concerns.text: Task T016b (timeout detection) is placed in Phase 3 (US1) but depends on the full pipeline execution logic defined in T023 (US2) and T031 (US3). The 'full pipeline' timeout constraint (SC-004) requires the aggregation of results from all networks, which only occurs after US2 (T023) and US3 (T031) are complete. Implementing this check in US1 creates a consumer-before-producer violation where the check runs before the full dataset aggregation exists.

Task T023 (aggregate sim_results.json) is listed in Phase 4 (US2) but explicitly depends on T016 (US1) completion. However, T016b (timeout logic) is also in Phase 3. If T016b is intended to monitor the *entire* pipeline (as per SC-004), it cannot be implemented within the US1 scope (T016) which only processes a single network or a subset. The dependency graph implies T023 must run before the final timeout check can be meaningful, yet T016b is scheduled earlier.

Tasks T044-T046 (US1) introduce higher-order metrics (motifs, spectral gap) into `src/topology.py`. Tasks T047-T048 (US2) then consume these new metrics in the regression pipeline. While the order is generally correct (Producer T044 before Consumer T047), T047 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). This is incorrect: T047 depends on the *output* of T044/T045. If T044 is not completed, T047 cannot run against the new schema. The [P] tag on T047 implies it can run independently of T044, violating the producer-consumer dependency.

Task T017b (SNAP list sorting and manual verification) is placed in Phase 3 (US1). However, the verification logic requires the *results* of the simulation (T014/T016) to be generated first. While T017b is listed after T016, the task description 'implement... comparison logic' suggests it might be a setup task. If it is an implementation task that runs the verification, it must strictly follow T016. If it is a setup task, it should be in Phase 2. The current placement is ambiguous regarding whether it produces the verification artifact or just the logic.

Task T016b description mentions 'log 'TIMEOUT' status... if any single network exceeds 6 hours'. This contradicts the semantic flow of SC-004 which defines the timeout against the 'full simulation and analysis pipeline for 10+ networks'. A single network timeout check is a different constraint. The task should be re-ordered or re-scoped to reflect that it monitors the *aggregate* pipeline time, which requires the completion of the aggregation step (T023).
